flags.AI_FLAG_BASIC: Rules out moves that would fail or do nothing: attacks the target is immune to (by type, or by abilities like Levitate, Volt Absorb, Flash Fire, Wonder Guard, Soundproof), status moves on a target that already has a status or is behind Safeguard, stat boosts that are already maxed, screens, hazards or weather that are already up, and similar. These get a big penalty (-10 or -12), so they are almost never picked.
flags.AI_FLAG_EVAL_ATTACK: Looks at damage. If a move's best damage roll would knock the target out it gets +4 (+6 if it is a Quick Attack-style first-strike move); any other attack that is not the hardest-hitting one gets -1. A 4x super-effective move gets +2 about 69% of the time, and Explosion, Focus Punch and Sucker Punch are usually marked down by 2.
flags.AI_FLAG_EXPERT: Move-by-move judgement for about 150 move effects. Examples: healing moves are favoured below 70% HP but get -8 when its Pokemon is faster than the target (as written in the code); stat-raising moves get +2 half the time at full HP and are usually marked down at 70% HP or less (always below 40%); Explosion becomes more likely as its own HP drops; draining moves are avoided against resistant targets. Most nudges are small (+/-1 to 3) and many are dice rolls.
flags.AI_FLAG_SETUP_FIRST_TURN: On the very first turn of the battle only, stat-raising, stat-lowering, screen, Substitute, Leech Seed, confusion and similar set-up or status moves get +2, 69% of the time.
flags.AI_FLAG_RISKY: Half the time gives +2 to gamble moves: sleep moves, Explosion/Self-Destruct, one-hit-KO moves, high-critical-hit moves, confusion, Metronome, Counter/Mirror Coat/Metal Burst, Destiny Bond, Swagger, Attract, Belly Drum, Focus Punch, Sucker Punch and the like.
flags.AI_FLAG_PRIORITIZE_EXTREMES: About 61% of the time gives +2 to moves whose damage the AI does not compare: status moves (power 0 or 1) and a list of special attacks (Explosion/Self-Destruct, Dream Eater, two-turn and recharge moves, Spit Up, Focus Punch, Sucker Punch, Superpower, Eruption-type, half-recoil moves). Fixed-damage and variable-power moves are compared in Gen 4, so they don't get this bonus. Despite the name it does not favour the strongest attack.
flags.AI_FLAG_BATON_PASS: Supports a Baton Pass plan when it has teammates left; only non-attacking moves are affected, and if it doesn't know Baton Pass this is skipped about 31% of the time. Set-up moves get +5 on the battle's first turn, -10 if its HP is under 60%, otherwise +1, and most of them also get +3 first. Protect gets +2 unless it was used last turn (-2). Baton Pass itself gets -2 on turn 1, then +1 to +3 once Attack or Sp. Atk is boosted.
flags.AI_FLAG_TAG_STRATEGY: Double-battle teamwork: avoids hitting its partner with spread moves the partner is weak to (e.g. Earthquake -10), favours weather, Gravity, Trick Room, Follow Me and Helping Hand when they suit both Pokemon, and gives small bonuses to super-effective or partner-boosted attacks. Always switched on in double battles.
flags.AI_FLAG_CHECK_HP: Picks moves that suit its own and the target's HP: above 70% HP it shies away from Explosion, healing, Rest, Destiny Bond, Flail-type and Endure-type moves; at 30-70% and below 30% it shies away from stat changes and set-up; against a low-HP target it avoids slow status and set-up moves. Each matching move gets -2 about 80% of the time.
flags.AI_FLAG_WEATHER: Meant to make the trainer open with a weather move (+5) on the first turn when that weather is not already active. As written, any move falls through to the Sunny Day check, so on the first turn every move gets +5 unless the sun is already out (inferred); the net effect is mostly that a weather move whose weather is already up loses out.
flags.AI_FLAG_HARRASSMENT: Half the time gives +2 to annoying moves: sleep, poison, paralysis, burn, confusion, stat-lowering moves, Leech Seed, Encore, Spite, Spikes / Toxic Spikes, Attract, Torment, Embargo, Knock Off, Captivate and similar.
flags.AI_FLAG_ROAMING_POKEMON: Not a trainer flag: used for roaming wild Pokemon, which simply run away unless trapped (Mean Look, a binding move, Shadow Tag, or Arena Trap without Levitate).
flags.AI_FLAG_SAFARI: Not a trainer flag: Safari Zone behaviour (watch or flee).
flags.AI_FLAG_CATCH_TUTORIAL: Not a trainer flag: the catching-tutorial Pokemon flees once the target is at 20% HP or less.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_CHECK_BAD_MOVE: Rules out moves that would fail or do nothing: attacks the target is immune to (by type, Levitate, Volt Absorb, Water Absorb, Flash Fire, Wonder Guard, Soundproof), status on an already-statused target, maxed stat boosts, screens or weather already up, and so on (-10 to -12). Emerald adds a few checks FireRed lacks, such as Safeguard and one-hit-KO immunity.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_TRY_TO_FAINT: Looks at damage. A move that would knock the target out (using a random 85-100% damage roll) gets +4, or +6 for a Quick Attack-style move, except Explosion; any other attack that is not the hardest-hitting gets -1. Emerald also gives a 4x super-effective move +2 about 69% of the time.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_CHECK_VIABILITY: Move-by-move judgement for most move effects (the Gen 3 ancestor of Gen 4's EXPERT). Healing moves are favoured below 70% HP but get -8 when its Pokemon is faster than the target (as written); stat boosts are favoured at high HP; Explosion is weighed against its own HP; many nudges are dice rolls.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_SETUP_FIRST_TURN: On the very first turn only, stat-changing, screen, Substitute, Leech Seed, confusion and similar moves get +2, 69% of the time.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_RISKY: Half the time gives +2 to gamble moves: sleep, Explosion, Mirror Move, one-hit-KO moves, high-crit moves, confusion, Metronome, Psywave, Counter/Mirror Coat, Destiny Bond, Swagger, Attract, Present, Belly Drum, Focus Punch, Revenge, Teeter Dance and similar.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_PREFER_POWER_EXTREMES: About 61% of the time gives +2 to moves whose damage is not compared: status moves, 0- or 1-power moves and a list of special effects (Explosion, Dream Eater, charge-up moves, Hyper Beam-type, Spit Up, Focus Punch, Superpower, Eruption, Overheat).
flags.AI_SCRIPT_PREFER_STRONGEST_MOVE: FireRed/LeafGreen's name for the same bit-5 script as Emerald's PREFER_POWER_EXTREMES. Despite the name, it gives +2 (about 61% of the time) only to moves whose damage is not compared, such as status moves and fixed-damage moves, not to the strongest attack.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_PREFER_BATON_PASS: Supports a Baton Pass plan when teammates remain; only moves whose damage isn't compared (mostly status moves) are affected, and without Baton Pass this is skipped about 31% of the time. FireRed just gives them +3 (about 92% of the time). Emerald adds a turn-based rule for set-up moves (+5 on the battle's first turn, -10 under 60% HP, otherwise +1), gives Protect +2 unless it was used last turn, and favours Baton Pass itself once Attack or Sp. Atk is boosted (-2 on turn 1).
flags.AI_SCRIPT_DOUBLE_BATTLE: Emerald double-battle teamwork: avoids Earthquake/Magnitude when they would hurt the partner, uses Skill Swap, Helping Hand and fire/electric moves sensibly around the partner's abilities. Emerald adds it automatically in doubles. In FireRed/LeafGreen the script is empty and is never added automatically.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_HP_AWARE: Picks moves that suit its own and the target's HP: above 70% HP it avoids Explosion, healing, Rest, Destiny Bond, Flail, Endure, Memento, Overheat; at 31-70% and at 30% or less it avoids stat changes and set-up; against a low-HP target it avoids slow status and set-up moves. Each match gets -2 about 80% of the time.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_TRY_SUNNY_DAY_START: Gives Sunny Day +5 on its Pokemon's first turn out. A check before that reads a leftover result instead of a fresh one (marked as a bug in the source), so whether it fires depends on earlier script state.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_UNKNOWN: FireRed/LeafGreen's name for bit 9: the same Sunny-Day-on-first-turn script as Emerald's TRY_SUNNY_DAY_START (+5), with the same check on a leftover result.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_ROAMING: Not a trainer flag: roaming wild Pokemon flee unless trapped.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_SAFARI: Not a trainer flag: Safari Zone Pokemon watch or randomly flee.
flags.AI_SCRIPT_FIRST_BATTLE: Not a trainer flag: the very first wild battle's Pokemon flees once the player's Pokemon is at 20% HP or less.
flags.AI_BASIC: Rules out moves a separate redundancy check marks as useless right now (the source comments name healing moves, weather moves and Dream Eater as examples) and status-only moves (sleep, poison, paralysis, Toxic) when the player already has a status or is behind Safeguard. Each gets a +10 penalty (in Crystal a higher score is worse).
flags.AI_SETUP: Half the time strongly favours stat-raising moves on its Pokemon's first turn out, and stat-lowering moves on the player's Pokemon's first turn out; otherwise discourages them about 88% of the time.
flags.AI_TYPES: Rules out moves the player's Pokemon is immune to, slightly favours super-effective attacks, and slightly discourages not-very-effective attacks if it has another damaging move of a different type.
flags.AI_OFFENSIVE: Discourages every move that does no damage.
flags.AI_SMART: Situation-specific rules for about 80 move effects. Examples: healing moves are strongly favoured below 25% HP (90% of the time) and discouraged above 50%; a first-strike move is strongly favoured when its Pokemon is slower and the move would KO; Thief is avoided; Reflect/Light Screen are avoided unless at full HP; Toxic and Leech Seed are avoided when the player is below 50% HP.
flags.AI_OPPORTUNIST: When its Pokemon is low on HP, stops wasting turns on stall moves (stat changes, screens, Substitute, Leech Seed and similar): always below 25% HP, half the time at 25-50%, never above 50%.
flags.AI_AGGRESSIVE: Works out which attack does the most damage and slightly discourages every other damaging move, except fixed-damage moves and reckless moves (Self-Destruct, Thrash-type, multi-hit moves).
flags.AI_CAUTIOUS: After its first turn, discourages residual moves (Mist, Leech Seed, Poison Powder, Stun Spore, Thunder Wave, Focus Energy, Bide, Poison Gas, Transform, Conversion, Substitute, Spikes) about 90% of the time (a documented bug can make it skip some).
flags.AI_STATUS: Rules out status moves and attacks that can't affect the player's Pokemon: poison moves on Poison types, and sleep/paralysis moves or attacks the target's type is immune to.
flags.AI_RISKY: Strongly favours any attack that would knock out the player's Pokemon. Self-Destruct/Explosion and one-hit-KO moves are left out of this at full HP and about 80% of the time otherwise, so despite the name it does not seek out gambles.

coach.aggression: 0-100, default 50: how much accuracy counts when picking an attack (100 ignores it, 0 counts it twice)
coach.patience: 0-100: the most HP it will have lost and still set up (boosts, Substitute, screens, weather)
coach.heal_line: 0-100: heal at or under this HP %, even if the next hit wouldn't knock it out
coach.risk_tolerance: 0-100: the lowest accuracy it calls when a surer attack is available
coach.tempo: 'finish' (priority only to finish) or 'any' (default: whenever it's the best attack)
